summary: Uses the Oculus Audio SDK to spatialize a mono input channel into stereo/spatial audio channels based on listener/source transforms and room parameters.
key_concepts: Oculus Audio CHOP is a Windows-only Oculus Audio SDK operator for spatializing audio in CHOP networks.
It takes a mono sound channel and creates spatialized stereo or spatial output channels from listener and source transforms.
Head Object represents the listener transform, while Source Object represents the emitting sound transform.
Range, source diameter, band hint, attenuation, reflections, and box-room parameters shape the perceived spatial audio result.
Audio Render CHOP is the broader spatial-audio alternative when an Oculus-specific SDK workflow is not required.

key_params.name: diameter
key_params.note: Virtual source diameter; 0 means point source

key_params.name: bandhint
key_params.note: None, wide-band, or narrow-band source hint

key_params.name: autoexportroot
key_params.note: Root path for automatic channel-name exports

key_params.name: exporttable
key_params.note: DAT table used by DAT table export methods

common_gotchas: Official docs list this operator as Windows-only.
The audio input is expected to be mono; this CHOP creates the spatialized stereo/output channels.
Head Object and Source Object must be COMPs with transform data, such as Geometry or Camera COMPs.
Band Hint changes quality/artifact tradeoffs; wide-band sources such as music/voice/noise differ from narrow-band tones.
Reflection/reverb parameters only matter when the corresponding reverb mode is enabled.
Use Audio Render CHOP for broader spatial audio workflows when the Oculus-specific SDK path is not desired.
